topic: How does defocused reflector gain loss impact link budget margins for SNR compared to conventional designs?
consensus_response: The defocused reflector system suffers from increased gain loss, compromising link budget margins and signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) stability. The average unit cell loss is around 4-5 dB, affecting the receiver's ability to distinguish signal from noise and reducing its sensitivity. This leads to decreased frequency agility and makes it challenging for the receiver to maintain a stable SNR in frequency reuse scenarios.
reference_context: The defocused reflector system has an average unit cell loss of around 4-5 dB, which affects link budget margins and SNR stability in conventional designs.
